- Q1'FY27 cash bridge as printed: collections 6.7 plus other inflows 1.2 = cash inflow 7.9; less construction and approval expenses 4.6, SG&A 1.6, brokerage 0.4 and taxes/other outflows 1.0, giving operating cash surplus before land of 0.3; after land advance/acquisition 1.3, approval cost 0.1 and interest payments 0.8, net debt increased by 1.9.
- CARE rating received on NCD issuance as A+; stable. Net debt history at Mar-22 to Jun-26 is printed as 5.2, 10.9, 11.6, 8.8, 2.0, 3.9 INR bn.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration risk - operations concentrated in Delhi-NCR, particularly Gurugram and Sohna, with significant reliance on residential projects — Any adverse change in local market dynamics, demand patterns or pricing trends could affect sales performance and financial results. Mitigated by diversifying across property categories and expanding into luxury housing and industrial township.
- Regulatory risk - complex and evolving approvals regime covering land acquisition, zoning, environmental clearances, building permits, RERA, taxation and local development authority regulations — Delays in obtaining approvals, changes in government policies, revisions to development norms or non-compliance may lead to project delays, increased costs, legal liabilities and reputational damage. Mitigated by dedicated legal and compliance teams, standardised processes, internal controls and periodic audits.
- Interest rate and funding risk - the capital-intensive business depends on external borrowings from banks and financial institutions for working capital and project financing — Rising borrowing and mortgage rates may reduce profitability and weaken property demand. Mitigated by an efficient execution model enabling faster completion and timely cash flow generation, plus portfolio diversification across property segments.
- Inflation and input cost risk - rising land acquisition costs and construction material prices — Shortages or cost escalation in materials, labour and equipment may disrupt project schedules and hurt profitability, operations and cash flows. Mitigated by timely procurement at competitive prices, strategic inventory planning for cement, steel and aluminium, and aluminium formwork technology.
- Macro-economic risk - economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures, interest rate movements and geopolitical uncertainties — These may adversely impact consumer sentiment, purchasing power and demand for real estate, constraining business growth and sales volumes. Mitigated by execution capability, sustained construction progress and disciplined inventory management.
- Manpower risk - labour shortages, work stoppages and disruptions in contract labour availability in a labour-intensive industry — Such disruptions may affect project execution, operational efficiency and financial performance. Mitigated through proactive workforce planning, recruitment and retention practices, compliance monitoring and competitive compensation.
- Climate risk - insufficient preparedness for climate-related challenges — May lead to financial losses, operational disruptions and constraints on strategic growth initiatives, and could adversely affect ESG performance, customer trust and investor confidence. Mitigated through environmental policies focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving water and waste management and sustainable procurement, supported by comprehensive ESG reporting and disclosure frameworks.

outlook.body:

outlook.body: Signatureglobal expanded its Delhi-NCR development footprint during FY 2025-26, operating 29 active project sites in Haryana (27 under construction and 2 recently launched). Two premium group-housing projects were launched during the year: Cloverdale SPR, an ultra-luxury high-rise in Sector 71 on the Southern Peripheral Road, Gurugram, and Sarvam at DXP Estate, a wellness-centric project on the Dwarka Expressway; 6.52 mn sqft of saleable area was launched in FY 2025-26 and approximately 2.3 mn sqft was added to the portfolio in the Sohna region. The Company entered large-scale commercial development through a 50:50 joint venture with Millennia Realtors Private Limited (RMZ Group) named Gurugram Commercity Limited, formed under a Securities Subscription and Purchase Agreement dated 14th February 2026 and completed on 30th March 2026, to develop a mixed-use project of office buildings, hotel(s) and retail (a design district) utilising approximately 3.94 million square feet of FSI in Sector 71 on the Southern Peripheral Road, Gurugram. In April 2026 the Company announced a collaboration with Tonino Lamborghini for a premium branded residence project in Sector 71, Gurugram, spread over 12.4 acres, marking the Italian brand's entry into Indian residential real estate. As of March 31, 2026 completed projects aggregated 12.60 million square feet of developable area with a further 5.30 million square feet under development; the combined portfolio stood at 53.3 mn sqft comprising 12.3 mn sqft ongoing, 19.8 mn sqft forthcoming and 21.2 mn sqft recently launched, with approximately 19.8 mn sqft of planned launches over the next 2-3 years. Forthcoming saleable-area potential by focus corridor is 17.8 mn sqft on SPR (Sector 71), 9.5 mn sqft on Dwarka Expressway and 7.5 mn sqft on the Sohna Elevated Corridor, based on best estimates as per current zoning regulations. Township projects were added at the Sohna Elevated Corridor and Manesar, and the Company acquired the balance 15.41% equity of Indeed Fincap Private Limited on 20th June 2025, making it a wholly owned subsidiary.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Residential accounts for 78.8% of the Indian real estate market in 2025, supported by urbanisation, an expanding middle-income population, increasing nuclear families and improved access to housing finance.
- Premiumisation is the defining trend in India's residential market - the share of luxury housing in total NCR residential sales rose to 58% in FY 2024-25 from 24% in FY21.
- NCR recorded the strongest residential price growth among India's top seven cities, with average selling prices up approximately 31% YoY in FY 2024-25 and a further 13% YoY in H1 FY 2025-26; price appreciation is expected to continue but the pace is likely to moderate over the medium term.
- Inventory absorption is healthy: Years-to-Sell improved to 0.6 year as of September 2025 from 1.7 years in March 2022, and is expected to remain at 0.6-0.7 year through March 2027.
- ICRA estimates NCR residential area sold to increase by 12-15% to 115-120 mn sqft in FY 2025-26.
- Infrastructure-led growth - metro expansions, the Dwarka Expressway, the Sohna-Gurugram Elevated Expressway, KMP Expressway and UER-II - is unlocking new development corridors and lifting capital values in the Company's micro-markets.
- Global Capability Centres accounted for 40% of office leasing and act as employment hubs that drive residential demand in surrounding micro-markets; NCR recorded 23% capital appreciation during 2025.
- Branded residences are a nascent but fast-growing asset class in India, globally commanding an average pricing premium of approximately 33% over comparable non-branded luxury developments, which is expected to support higher sales realisations and improved profitability for developers.
- Average sales realisation rose to INR 15,250 per sqft in FY 2025-26 from INR 12,457 per sqft in FY 2024-25, reflecting the shift in product mix towards premium housing.
- Government support through PMAY and RERA-led transparency, plus improved mortgage penetration and rising institutional participation, continue to underpin housing demand.
- Combined portfolio of 53.3 mn sqft as of FY 2025-26, comprising 12.3 mn sqft of ongoing projects, 19.8 mn sqft of saleable area in the forthcoming pipeline and 21.2 mn sqft of recently launched projects.
- Approximately 19.8 mn sqft of planned launches over the next 2-3 years, providing visibility for future growth.
- 6.52 mn sqft of saleable area launched in FY 2025-26; 5.4 mn sqft of area sold in FY 2025-26 across 2,124 units.
- 17.9 mn sqft of saleable area completed and delivered up to March 31, 2026; 38,838 total units sold as of March 31, 2026.
- Saleable area potential for forthcoming projects in the focus areas: 17.8 mn sqft on SPR (Sector 71), 9.5 mn sqft on Dwarka Expressway and 7.5 mn sqft on the Sohna Elevated Corridor, based on best estimates as per current zoning regulations.
- Approximately 2.3 mn sqft portfolio addition during FY 2025-26 in the Sohna region.

one-line thesis: Signature Global reported record PAT driven by a one-off JV transaction with RMZ, while operationally pivoting toward premium segments with 20%+ price realization growth and a near-zero net debt balance sheet. The company guides for aggressive new launches (INR 15,000 Cr) in FY27, leveraging a massive 40 Mn sq ft pipeline to capitalize on Gurgaon's acute shortage of deliverable inventory.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 26 Bn (+YoY growth implied by completion of 3.75 Mn sq ft); EBITDA Margin: 9-10% (Operating); PAT: INR 11 Bn+ (Reported, includes ~INR 12.5 Bn one-off from RMZ JV transaction); Normalized PAT: ~INR 2-3 Bn (implied by operating cash flow); Order Book: ~INR 80-85 Bn (Inventory + Recent Launches); Net Debt: ~INR 2 Bn (Near Zero). One-offs: INR 12.5 Bn gain from RMZ JV land contribution skewed reported PAT.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting INR 50 Bn recognition (requires INR 60-65 Bn completion); Margin: Stable operating margins expected; Order Inflow: Targeting INR 100 Bn sales; Capex/Commissioning: INR 35-40 Bn total for RMZ JV over 4-5 years (50% share off-balance sheet).
order book & pipeline: Total pipeline GDV > INR 70,000 Cr across 40 Mn sq ft (18 Mn completed, 12 Mn nearing completion, 21 Mn launched, 19 Mn land bank). Immediate sellable inventory valued at ~INR 80-85 Bn.
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential (Affordable to Premium): Core driver, 21+ Mn sq ft launched in last 8 quarters. Commercial (JV with RMZ): 5.5 Mn sq ft in Sector 71 (4-4.5 Mn office, rest retail/hotel), build-to-lease/sell hybrid. Branded Residences: Tie-up with Tonino Lamborghini for 2 Mn sq ft premium project.
growth verticals / optionality: Monetization of 19 Mn sq ft land bank; Expansion in Sohna and Manesar (plotted/industrial); Premiumization mix shift driving per-sq-ft realization above INR 15,000; Potential for further strategic JVs for yield assets.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Profit Margin ~30%; EBITDA Margin 9-10%. Realization per sq ft crossed INR 15,000 (+20% YoY) driven by product mix shift to premium group housing and market escalation. Construction costs managed via steady completion pipeline.
capex / expansion: FY27 BD spend expected to be significant (pipeline >INR 7 Bn already identified for Sohna/Manesar). RMZ JV requires INR 35-40 Bn total capex over 4-5 years, funded via JV-level debt and equal equity infusion (INR 15-20 Bn Signature share), kept off consolidated debt.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Debt reduction (achieved near-zero net debt). Priority 2: Business Development (land acquisition in Sohna/Manesar). Priority 3: Funding JV equity commitments. No dividend guidance explicitly detailed beyond historical norms.
risks & watch-items: Execution slippage on completions (history of rain/NGT delays); Macro headwinds affecting affordable segment demand; Concentration risk in Gurgaon/NCR; Dependency on pre-sales (40% target) for new launches to fund construction.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; Emphasizes 'once bitten twice shy' regarding aggressive guidance but highlights strong liquidity; Bullish on Gurgaon supply-demand imbalance supporting price hikes.
non-obvious takeaways: The reported PAT surge is almost entirely non-recurring (JV transaction), masking a modest operating profit year; The company is strategically exiting 'build-to-yield' risks by partnering with RMZ for commercial assets while retaining 100% ownership of the residential component on the same land.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Residential accounts for 78.8% of the Indian real estate market in 2025, supported by urbanisation, an expanding middle-income population, increasing nuclear families and improved access to housing finance.
- Premiumisation is the defining trend in India's residential market - the share of luxury housing in total NCR residential sales rose to 58% in FY 2024-25 from 24% in FY21.
- NCR recorded the strongest residential price growth among India's top seven cities, with average selling prices up approximately 31% YoY in FY 2024-25 and a further 13% YoY in H1 FY 2025-26; price appreciation is expected to continue but the pace is likely to moderate over the medium term.
- Inventory absorption is healthy: Years-to-Sell improved to 0.6 year as of September 2025 from 1.7 years in March 2022, and is expected to remain at 0.6-0.7 year through March 2027.
- ICRA estimates NCR residential area sold to increase by 12-15% to 115-120 mn sqft in FY 2025-26.
- Infrastructure-led growth - metro expansions, the Dwarka Expressway, the Sohna-Gurugram Elevated Expressway, KMP Expressway and UER-II - is unlocking new development corridors and lifting capital values in the Company's micro-markets.
- Global Capability Centres accounted for 40% of office leasing and act as employment hubs that drive residential demand in surrounding micro-markets; NCR recorded 23% capital appreciation during 2025.
- Branded residences are a nascent but fast-growing asset class in India, globally commanding an average pricing premium of approximately 33% over comparable non-branded luxury developments, which is expected to support higher sales realisations and improved profitability for developers.
- Average sales realisation rose to INR 15,250 per sqft in FY 2025-26 from INR 12,457 per sqft in FY 2024-25, reflecting the shift in product mix towards premium housing.
- Government support through PMAY and RERA-led transparency, plus improved mortgage penetration and rising institutional participation, continue to underpin housing demand.
- Combined portfolio of 53.3 mn sqft as of FY 2025-26, comprising 12.3 mn sqft of ongoing projects, 19.8 mn sqft of saleable area in the forthcoming pipeline and 21.2 mn sqft of recently launched projects.
- Approximately 19.8 mn sqft of planned launches over the next 2-3 years, providing visibility for future growth.
- 6.52 mn sqft of saleable area launched in FY 2025-26; 5.4 mn sqft of area sold in FY 2025-26 across 2,124 units.
- 17.9 mn sqft of saleable area completed and delivered up to March 31, 2026; 38,838 total units sold as of March 31, 2026.
- Saleable area potential for forthcoming projects in the focus areas: 17.8 mn sqft on SPR (Sector 71), 9.5 mn sqft on Dwarka Expressway and 7.5 mn sqft on the Sohna Elevated Corridor, based on best estimates as per current zoning regulations.
- Approximately 2.3 mn sqft portfolio addition during FY 2025-26 in the Sohna region.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Signatureglobal expanded its Delhi-NCR development footprint during FY 2025-26, operating 29 active project sites in Haryana (27 under construction and 2 recently launched). Two premium group-housing projects were launched during the year: Cloverdale SPR, an ultra-luxury high-rise in Sector 71 on the Southern Peripheral Road, Gurugram, and Sarvam at DXP Estate, a wellness-centric project on the Dwarka Expressway; 6.52 mn sqft of saleable area was launched in FY 2025-26 and approximately 2.3 mn sqft was added to the portfolio in the Sohna region. The Company entered large-scale commercial development through a 50:50 joint venture with Millennia Realtors Private Limited (RMZ Group) named Gurugram Commercity Limited, formed under a Securities Subscription and Purchase Agreement dated 14th February 2026 and completed on 30th March 2026, to develop a mixed-use project of office buildings, hotel(s) and retail (a design district) utilising approximately 3.94 million square feet of FSI in Sector 71 on the Southern Peripheral Road, Gurugram. In April 2026 the Company announced a collaboration with Tonino Lamborghini for a premium branded residence project in Sector 71, Gurugram, spread over 12.4 acres, marking the Italian brand's entry into Indian residential real estate. As of March 31, 2026 completed projects aggregated 12.60 million square feet of developable area with a further 5.30 million square feet under development; the combined portfolio stood at 53.3 mn sqft comprising 12.3 mn sqft ongoing, 19.8 mn sqft forthcoming and 21.2 mn sqft recently launched, with approximately 19.8 mn sqft of planned launches over the next 2-3 years. Forthcoming saleable-area potential by focus corridor is 17.8 mn sqft on SPR (Sector 71), 9.5 mn sqft on Dwarka Expressway and 7.5 mn sqft on the Sohna Elevated Corridor, based on best estimates as per current zoning regulations. Township projects were added at the Sohna Elevated Corridor and Manesar, and the Company acquired the balance 15.41% equity of Indeed Fincap Private Limited on 20th June 2025, making it a wholly owned subsidiary.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [FY27 guidance] The deck sets FY27E guidance of INR 150 bn of launches (estimated booking value of projects launched or proposed to be launched), INR 100 bn pre-sales, INR 50 bn collections and INR 50 bn revenue recognition, against FY26A of 107, 82, 40 and 26 respectively; Q1'FY27 delivered 44, 20, 7 and 6, and the deck says it achieved c.20% of the sales guidance for the year.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
